headline: The same ladder shipped as components instead of values: no lane gains anything, and `@yak/solid` loses an order of magnitude, because a component crossing a module boundary is the one thing folding cannot rewrite.

microbench.why: The leaders are inside noise of each other — `next-yak-nofold` at 1.32M renders/s, `cn` at 1.31M, `vanilla` at 1.31M — because collapsing three wrappers into one element is what all of them already do. `next-yak` at 1.22M merges the chain's attrs and style processors once at construction, so three levels render as one component. `yak-solid` at 225,000 cannot: `styled(Component)` keeps the runtime wrapper, and 4.42 of its 5.80 ms per render is Solid instantiating that component per instance, against 0.792 ms of yak's own work.

autocannon.why: `vanilla` and `next-yak-nofold` tie near 1,080 req/s with `next-yak` at 1,070 — a three-way tie inside the measurement's spread. `yak-solid` at 199 req/s and `emotion` at 348 are the lanes doing per-instance work in the request path.

attribution.why: `cn` at 0.842 ms leads, with `cnfast` at 0.898 ms and `vanilla` at 1.04 ms — three levels of merging cost a caching merger almost nothing once the strings repeat. `next-yak` at 1.07 ms books 0.428 ms of lib for its one collapsed wrapper. `yak-solid`'s 5.80 ms is 76% framework, the cost of the component Solid must build for each element rather than of yak resolving styles.

hydrate.why: `vanilla-solid` at 43.1 ms leads a React field that starts at 48.1 ms, a gap small enough to be framework noise rather than mechanism. `yak-solid` at 65.6 ms walks the unfolded wrappers again; `goober` at 141 ms and `styled-components` at 138 ms inject their sheets while attaching.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

inp.why: `yak-solid` at 4.3 ms and `vanilla-solid` at 4.4 ms against roughly 7.5 ms for the React lanes, with React writing nothing on this pass. `goober` at 10.8 ms and `emotion` at 10.6 ms re-run the chain per level.

mount.why: `vanilla-solid` mounts in 24.2 ms and `yak-solid` in 46.1 ms — the 22 ms between them is the wrapper chain, the same cost the SSR number exposes. The React lanes span 72.9 ms to 107 ms with layout dominating.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane. Three component levels produce one element with one class list, so nothing reaches the style engine differently.

payload.why: `vanilla` is the floor at 3,164 gz B and `next-yak` adds 914 B of runtime for the same markup. `yak-solid` at 9,175 B carries Solid's runtime and an id namespace per unfolded instance, so this case shows the hydration-key cost at its worst. `cn` at 16,668 B is the heaviest. The next-yak css-prop lanes have no cell here: the css prop resolves only top-scope values, so a fragment cannot reach a component through a prop.

nsweep.why: `vanilla` and `next-yak-nofold` hold 3.04 ms at 4,000 instances and `next-yak` 3.49 ms — all flat, because the chain collapses before render. `yak-solid` at 20.2 ms has the case's only real slope.

crossCase: The identical declarations as the Example `button-variants`, exported as components rather than style values. `next-yak` moves 2.12M to 1.22M renders/s — it still collapses the chain at construction, so the API costs it 42%. `yak-solid` moves 5.08M to 225,000: the value form folds away completely and the component form leaves a Solid component with its own reactive scope on every instance.
